title: The Star That Vanished—3 Telescopes Saw It Die in Real Time
hook: A star the size of a thousand suns just winked out of existence, and no one can explain why the light simply stopped.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea that a star can just 'turn off' defies basic physics and triggers deep existential dread—perfect for the cosmic horror audience.

title: The Asteroid That Has a Face—And It's Staring at Earth
hook: NASA's deep-space probe captured a formation on an asteroid that looks exactly like a human face—and it's aimed directly at us.
why_this_can_go_viral: Face pareidolia goes viral instantly, and combining it with a potential threat from space creates irresistible click-through.

title: The Signal That Came From a Dead Galaxy—Light-Years Past the Edge
hook: Astronomers picked up a repeating radio burst from a galaxy that went dark 2 billion years ago—something is still transmitting.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of a signal from a dead source plays on the creepiest trope—'the call is coming from inside the house,' but cosmic scale.

title: The Dark Matter That Is Slowly Shredding Earth's Magnetic Field
hook: A dense patch of dark matter is drifting through the solar system, and it's already peeling away our magnetic shield from the inside.
why_this_can_go_viral: Dark matter is already mysterious, but framing it as an active, invisible threat to Earth gives it a horror-movie urgency.

title: The Classified Russian Space Station That Found a Door in Orbit
hook: Declassified cosmonaut logs describe a perfectly rectangular hatch floating in low Earth orbit—and it opened when they approached.
why_this_can_go_viral: The fusion of classified Soviet space programs with a literal 'door in space' triggers both conspiracy curiosity and sci-fi wonder.

title: The Black Hole That Is Eating a Galaxy—But Leaving the Stars Intact
hook: A supermassive black hole is devouring a neighboring galaxy, but every star remains perfectly in orbit around nothing—a ghost galaxy.
why_this_can_go_viral: The visual of stars orbiting empty space is haunting and creates a 'skeleton galaxy' metaphor that sticks with viewers.

title: The Fermi Paradox Answer: We Live in a Cosmic Desert—And Something Is Blocking the Exit
hook: New calculations show that a massive gravitational barrier surrounds our local cluster—nothing gets in, nothing gets out.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea that we're trapped in a cosmic prison is a viral existential punch—combines Fermi paradox with sci-fi horror.

title: The Star That Erupted With a Plasma Wave—And It's Headed Straight for Us
hook: A Wolf-Rayet star 8,000 light-years away just unleashed a plasma wave traveling at relativistic speed—Earth is in its path.
why_this_can_go_viral: Imminent cosmic doom is an evergreen viral trigger—'something is coming for us' always drives engagement.

title: The Secret NASA Briefing on the Asteroid That Changed Color Overnight
hook: NASA held an emergency closed-door meeting when an asteroid shifted from red to blue in under 12 hours—something painted it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Color change on a cosmic scale is impossible by natural means—implies intelligence, which drives massive conspiracy interest.

title: The Dark Matter That Leaked Into the Solar System—And Warped Every Orbit
hook: An invisible cloud of dark matter passed through the inner solar system in 2017, and every planet wobbled—no one told the public.
why_this_can_go_viral: A hidden catastrophe that already happened—and we weren't told—is a classic viral conspiracy hook.

title: The Comet That Carried a Perfectly Cut Crystal—Geometry Impossible in Nature
hook: A diamond-like crystal with 18 faces was found inside a comet sample—no natural process creates that symmetry.
why_this_can_go_viral: Impossible geometry triggers the 'ancient alien artifact' reflex, a proven viral driver in the cosmic niche.

title: The Black Hole That's Older Than the Universe—A Paradox at the Center of a Galaxy
hook: A black hole with a mass of 12 billion suns formed just 800 million years after the Big Bang—it should not exist.
why_this_can_go_viral: Time paradoxes always go viral—'older than the universe' is a mind-bending hook that stops the scroll.

title: The Classified Space Plane That Flew for 780 Days—No One Knows What It Did
hook: The US military's X-37B space plane stayed in orbit for over two years—and the only thing that came back was a sealed container.
why_this_can_go_viral: Secret military space missions with unknown payloads are conspiracy gold—the secrecy itself drives curiosity.

title: The Signal That Matched the Prime Numbers—And Came From a Rogue Planet
hook: A rogue planet ejected from its star system is broadcasting prime numbers—the universal sign of intelligence—on a loop.
why_this_can_go_viral: Prime numbers are the 'calling card' of intelligence—combining that with a drifting, homeless planet is cinematic horror.

title: The Extinction Event That Happened in the Ocean—And Left No Land Trace
hook: A massive extinction struck the deep ocean 100 million years ago—every sea creature died, but the land was untouched. We don't know what caused it.
why_this_can_go_viral: A selective extinction event that targeted only the ocean is deeply unsettling and raises questions about targeted cosmic forces.

title: The Dark Matter That Hummed a Melody—Perfect Pitch, No Source
hook: Scientists detected a perfect B-flat note emanating from a cloud of dark matter—a sound with no physical origin.
why_this_can_go_viral: The universe 'singing' is a poetic and eerie concept—music from nothing triggers both wonder and unease.

title: The Star That Has a Ring Around It—Made of Something That Absorbs All Light
hook: A star 1,500 light-years away is encircled by a perfectly dark ring that absorbs every wavelength—a structure, not a cloud.
why_this_can_go_viral: Anything that suggests a Dyson Sphere or alien megastructure is an instant viral trigger in the cosmic niche.

title: The Comet That Left a Trail of Antimatter—Annihilating Everything in Its Path
hook: A comet's tail contained positrons that annihilated dust particles as it passed—a trail of tiny explosions across the solar system.
why_this_can_go_viral: Antimatter is already a buzzword—combining it with a comet that 'destroys what it touches' creates dramatic visual tension.

title: The Black Hole That Is Emitting Structured Light—A Beacon from the Abyss
hook: A black hole is firing focused beams of light in a repeating pattern—like a lighthouse from the edge of existence.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'lighthouse from hell' metaphor is instantly gripping—implies intent, navigation, or warning from the abyss.

title: The Classified Apollo Mission That Found Footprints—Not Human, Not Animal
hook: Declassified Apollo 17 surface photos show a chain of perfectly spaced, three-toed footprints near the Taurus-Littrow valley.
why_this_can_go_viral: Footprints on the moon that aren't human is the ultimate classified lunar conspiracy—drives massive debate and shares.
